title: Granular burn allocator & pricing sensitivity lab
body:
Purpose:
This is a working lab for a fine-grained budgeting allocator that ties per-feature micro-budgets to candidate hiring plans and pricing sensitivity triggers. The goal is a compact, operational playbook (and small spreadsheet) we can use to decide: when to hire, when to lean on contractor/apprentice pools, and which pricing levers to twitch for short-term runway preservation.

Executive summary (one paragraph):
We model three near-term scenarios that combine token demand, GPU constraint, and price pressure. The design leans on (a) a micro-bucket allocator per product vertical, (b) a priority-based headcount queue (apprentice -> contractor -> senior hire), and (c) automated triggers that flip pricing tiers or throttle non-critical routes. Early results show that a 10% reallocation of micro-budgets from low-value features plus a temporary 12% on-route price uplift recovers ~6 weeks of runway under the medium stress case.

Key assumptions (sticky):
- Monthly baseline burn (op-ex + infra): $6.1M (May baseline).
- Token mix: 65% embeddings, 25% short chat, 10% long-form gen.
- GPU cost sensitivity: +20% if higher performance GPUs are forced (spot shortage).
- Average realized price elasticity per cohort: Enterprise -0.02, Midmarket -0.07, PLG -0.15.
- Hiring lead times: senior 8-12 weeks, mid 6-8 weeks, apprentice/contractor 2-4 weeks.

Micro-bucket allocator logic (sketch):
1) Each feature gets a micro-budget share = feature-weight * product-allocation.
2) Feature-weight combines: revenue-attached-score (0-1), latency-sensitivity (0-1), strategic-score (0-1).
3) Rebalance window: weekly. If a feature draws >120% of its micro-budget for two consecutive weeks, it enters throttling or pricing test.

Scenarios (high level):
- BASE (S0): steady demand, no price change, GPU stable. Monthly incremental burn: +$0.0M.
- SURGE-CONSTRAINED (S1): +25% token demand, GPU mix shifts +15% cost, PLG cohort suffers 20% churn if price rises >10%. Net monthly incremental burn: +$1.5M.
- PRICE-SHOCK (S2): external price pressure increases infra costs +30% and enterprise spends contractually sticky; revenue flat. Net monthly incremental burn: +$2.3M and lower elasticity benefits.

Scenario outputs (simple indicators):
- S0 runway delta: 0 weeks (reference).
- S1 runway delta: -5 to -8 weeks depending on micro-bucket reallocation aggressiveness.
- S2 runway delta: -9 to -14 weeks; requires combined hiring freeze + pricing uplift + apprentice surge to recover to within -4 weeks.

Sample micro-budget table (rows are CSV: feature, allocation_usd_month, weight_rev, weight_latency, weight_strat):
(see budget_table field for same table in CSV rows)

Headcount coupling rules (prioritized):
1) Freeze senior external hires in S1/S2 unless critical revenue impact > $250k ARR in 3 months.
2) Convert 30% of open IC requisitions to 12-week apprenticeships if time-to-impact < 6 weeks.
3) Use contractor pool for burst-capacity (limited to 14% of monthly burn to cap contingency costs).
4) Restore senior hiring only when rolling 4-week incremental burn < $150k.

Pricing levers (order of preference):
- Non-intrusive: introduce tiered usage caps with opt-in burst packs (PLG).
- Moderate: temporary per-route surcharge for long-form generations during peak windows.
- Aggressive: enterprise contract repricing aligned to committed throughput (only with sales sign-off).

Decision triggers (operational):
- If weekly realized token burn > 115% of forecast for 3/4 weeks -> enact micro-bucket emergency throttle and move 10% allocation from low-value features.
- If monthly infra cost delta > +12% -> open hiring freeze and simulate contractor/apprentice substitution.
- If realized churn in PLG cohort > 8% after a pricing uplift -> rollback uplift; escalate to GTM for messaging.

Quick numeric heuristics (for ops):
- Apprentice ramp ROI threshold: cost of apprentice over 12 weeks < 40% of projected revenue risk from unshipped features.
- Contractor cap: incremental contractor spend should not exceed 14% of monthly op-ex without explicit exec sign-off.

Action items / next steps (owners):
- Build a 12-week rolling simulator that consumes per-route token telemetry and outputs delta-runway (owner: Maya Brooks, due 2026-06-28).
- Prototype an on-route surcharge experiment for long-form generation with 3% uplift, 2-week A/B (owner: Ethan Zhao, due 2026-07-05).
- Draft a candidate apprentice job description and quick-hire checklist (owner: Priya Rao, due 2026-06-23).
- Add micro-buckets to cost reporting dashboard and expose feature-weight metrics (owner: finance eng team, linked: github:repo/cost-models#12).

Notes to self (informal):
- Keep the micro-buckets small and reversible. Operational overhead kills the signal.
- Prefer soft nudges (caps, opt-in packs) over blunt price hikes on PLG.
- Document every micro-lever test in Confluence (confluence:FIN-BURN-LAB-2026).

Appendix: quick sensitivity thought experiment (text):
- If we reassign 10% of micro-budgets from 4 bottom-decile features to runway reserve and simultaneously deploy a 6% temporary surcharge on peak long-gen windows, the model predicts reducing S1 runway loss from -6 weeks to -2 weeks (median). This depends heavily on PLG elasticity; if PLG sensitivity is -0.25 instead of -0.15, the same surcharge loses net revenue.

End of doc.
